title: Federal judge calls Flock 'indiscriminate mass surveillance'
why_read: A legal ruling on mass surveillance technology (automated license plate readers) with real implications for privacy law and tech policy.
analysis: This concerns a federal judge's ruling characterizing Flock Safety's automated license plate reader network as indiscriminate mass surveillance, which is significant for engineers working on or around surveillance tech, policy, or privacy-preserving systems. It's less about novel engineering and more about legal and societal consequences of widely deployed camera/AI systems. Still relevant to technologists who build or evaluate such systems and care about their societal impact.
